tool.name: Annotate
tool.command:
mkdir pycytominer_output &&
## Since the profiles and platemat headers are input as integers, they need to be converted in a a string columns_headers1=`head -n1 "$profiles" | cut -d, -f'$profiles_joiner'` && columns_headers2=`head -n1 "$platemap" | cut -d, -f'$platemap_joiner'` &&
pycytominer annotate
--profiles '$profiles' --output_file './pycytominer_output/output.csv' --output_type 'csv' --platemap '$platemap' ## "Metadata_" need to be add in front of the platemap header name to be read as input --join_on "Metadata_\$columns_headers2, \$columns_headers1"
&& cp './pycytominer_output/output.csv' '$output'

param.name: profiles
param.label: Input cell-profiling table
param.help: Table with features extracted from biological images

param.name: profiles_joiner
param.label: Column describing the wells
param.help: Column with well values in the cell-profiling table (i.e. Metadata_Well)

param.name: platemap
param.label: Input platemap table
param.help: Table with platempa information such a treatment, celline and concentration tested

param.name: platemap_joiner
param.label: Column describing the wells
param.help: Column with well values in the platemap (i.e. Metadata_well_position)

tool.help:
**What it does**
**Pycytominer annotate** joins a plate map file onto the well profiles, adding columns such as treatment, cell line, and concentration. The plate map is a CSV (or any tabular format) where each row describes one well.
Documentation: https://pycytominer.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html
